title: GraphQL Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Ask for one field
entries.summary: A schema names allowed fields. The resolver supplies a value for greeting.
notes: A query can only ask for fields declared in the schema.

entries.name: Choose part of an object
entries.summary: The query picks title and leaves out pages. The resolver still holds both fields.
notes: GraphQL object fields need a selection of their inner fields.

entries.name: Give a field an input
entries.summary: An argument supplies a value to a field. The resolver receives it in an object.
notes: The input must match the argument type.

entries.name: Keep query text and values apart
entries.summary: A variable lets one query be reused with different values. Its value is supplied separately.
notes: A declared required variable must be supplied.

entries.name: Read several objects
entries.summary: Square brackets describe a list type. The query selects title for each book.
notes: The list item shape must match the schema type.

entries.name: Give results different names
entries.summary: Aliases name two uses of the same field so both results can appear together.
notes: Two different arguments on one field need distinct response names.

entries.name: Reuse a field selection
entries.summary: A fragment gives a group of fields a name. The query spreads that group onto a Book.
notes: A fragment has to apply to the type at that position.

entries.name: Use a named set of choices
entries.summary: An enum limits a value to named choices. GREEN is a schema label, not arbitrary text.
notes: The resolver result must match an enum value.

entries.name: Ask for a change
entries.summary: A mutation names a write action. This local example changes one in-memory score.
notes: The resolver must implement the change; declaring a mutation alone does not save data.

entries.name: Require a value
entries.summary: The exclamation mark means a field must not be null. This resolver breaks that rule, so GraphQL reports an error.
notes: Use non-null only when the resolver can honour that promise.

entries.name: Choose fields with a flag
entries.summary: The include directive can choose whether a field is requested. The flag is false here.
notes: The directive input is Boolean, not the text "true" or "false".

entries.name: Group several inputs
entries.summary: An input type groups values sent into a mutation. It is separate from an output object type.
notes: This example returns the title only; a real resolver needs storage to save a book.
